command: Build core, Prefect, SQL, SQLModel, FastAPI, and the separate worker-plugin wheels; install them into a fresh Python 3.11 environment from the locked requirements; run with PYTHONPATH unset and pytest pythonpath disabled: python -m pytest -o pythonpath= -q tests/prefect -m prefect, then python -m pytest -o pythonpath= -q tests/fastapi/test_managed_application_0_56.py::test_managed_headless_and_http_command_semantics_match.
result: Installed-wheel Prefect/PostgreSQL suite: 41 passed in 49.72s with no skips. Installed-wheel headless/FastAPI parity: 1 passed in 0.53s.
assertions: Core, Prefect, SQL, SQLModel, FastAPI, and the worker-backend plugin resolved from the fresh environment installed wheels with PYTHONPATH unset.
All Prefect contract, recovery, security, schedule, lifecycle, Process-worker, and live PostgreSQL tests ran without environment-gated skips.

The suite includes separate Process-worker execution, PostgreSQL crash/effect recovery, source-staging and report-publication cancellation, remote terminal disagreement, and the live multiprocess retirement crash/retry and rollback campaign.

The installed-wheel suite includes a real Process worker hard-killed after the durable result-publication row commits but before artifact-bearing report publication returns; it verifies retained durable artifact files, pending publication across the crash, recovery from the same report snapshot, and no repeated PostgreSQL effect.

The installed-wheel suite also restarts Prefect at the exact remote-pause/retired-state-CAS cut and hard-kills a Process worker during a partial artifact staging write; recovery preserves the closed admission gate, removes the abandoned temporary file, writes a complete artifact, and records one PostgreSQL effect.

The suite rotates the environment-backed PostgreSQL sink credential after durable dispatch and before worker claim; only the credential alias is in the accepted snapshot, and the worker completes using a dedicated least-privilege role.
The existing headless and FastAPI managed-route parity test passed from the installed package environment.

The installed-wheel suite stops the PostgreSQL-backed Prefect API after the Process worker commits a sink effect and stores its successful report but before host finalization. Authorized status keeps the canonical run state and reports remote orchestration unavailable; restarting the same API database lets the held worker finalize once with one effect and one completed attempt.

runtime.prefect_server: Separately supervised API process backed by per-test PostgreSQL databases
runtime.worker_backend_plugin: Separately built and installed etlantic-phase058-test-worker-plugin 0.1.0 wheel

source_sha256_method: SHA-256 over sorted repository-relative source paths and file bytes, with NUL separators.
limitations: This is a local clean-wheel qualification campaign, not remote CI evidence or a production support commitment.
Only CPython 3.11.15, Prefect 3.7.8, PostgreSQL 16.13, and the Process pool were exercised; other versions, operating systems, hosting modes, and work pools remain unqualified.

The partial-effect fault is an integration fixture, not a production or third-party connector conformance result. Broader connector behavior, remaining outage and authority-rotation combinations, bounded deployment orphan cleanup, remote CI evidence, and the integrated release decision remain open.

ci_configuration.database_service: Local PostgreSQL 16.13; per-test SQLModel rows and Prefect databases were cleaned.
ci_configuration.server_process: Separate Prefect API process with PostgreSQL persistence

cleanup: The test suite used unique tenant, workspace, submission, deployment, and database identities; scoped test data was removed by the fixtures.
The shared local PostgreSQL service and the temporary installed-wheel environment were left intact; the suite stopped its per-test Prefect servers and dropped their dedicated databases.
